artifacts.synopsis: TE Merriam appealed his conviction by Tennessee Valley Presbytery on charges of violating ordination vows, including being contumacious toward brethren, failing to maintain church peace, and lacking exemplary piety. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error by the lower court and affirming TVP's procedures and judgment.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission found that the Judicial Commission of Korean Capital Presbytery did not follow proper procedures under BCO 32 and 34 in adjudicating charges against appellant TE Sang Soo Ryoo. Specifically, no indictment was ever properly served on the accused, and there was no clear record of proceedings. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with full compliance to BCO 32 and 34 procedures.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Sung Keon Kim appealed his deposition after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission conducted judicial process without serving an indictment and without an adequate record of the proceeding. The SJC sustained the procedural challenge, held that BCO 32 and 34 had not been followed, and remanded for a new trial under those chapters.

artifacts.title: Meaning of 'emergency' and validity of supermajority threshold for called presbytery meeting
artifacts.disposition: advice given — procedure in conflict with BCO 13-12

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that 'emergency' carries its plain dictionary meaning and that requiring concurrence of six of eight officers before calling a special meeting violates BCO 13-12 by overriding the rights of the smaller group entitled to call such meetings.
